name: ChatGPT
tagline: General AI assistant for writing, coding, research, images, and workflows

pricing.notes: Official OpenAI help/pricing checked 2026-07-30; ChatGPT Plus remains listed at $20/month.

verdictSummary: You can build a chat UI over APIs, but you cannot solo-recreate the model, multimodal stack, tools, memory/product layer, safety systems, and scale.
coreLoopDIY: Build a chat interface that calls OpenAI/Anthropic/local models, stores conversations, and adds file upload/tools.
requirements: LLM API key or local model
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for access to a continuously improving platform, not a textarea and send button.

priorArt.name: Open WebUI

notes: Obvious but necessary no; helps calibrate model-vs-wrapper products.
prompt:
Honest answer: you cannot rebuild ChatGPT. The product is a frontier model
plus tools, apps, and infrastructure; no prompt gets you a model. If you use
voice, images, agents, or memory weekly, keep paying.

But if what you actually use is text chat, a thin client on the API is a
real build, and light users often spend under $5/month in tokens:

- A local web chat app: Node + Express + better-sqlite3, one page with a
  streaming reply pane (SSE), a model picker, and a conversation sidebar.
- Calls the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs with keys from .env; system prompt
  editable per conversation.
- Conversations stored in SQLite with FTS5 search; export any thread to
  Markdown.
- File upload for text and PDF (pdf-parse), contents go straight into the
  context window, no vector database.
- A usage footer: tokens and estimated cost per conversation and per month,
  computed from the usage field in API responses, so I can compare my real
  spend against the $20 flat fee.
- Localhost only, no accounts, no telemetry beyond the API calls themselves.
- What you will NOT have: image generation, voice mode, browsing agents,
  memory, and the mobile apps. That gap is the subscription.
- README: where to get keys and links to current per-token pricing.
